content.json:
# AKS Desktop — usage & health

Built from the `customEvents` emitted by `plugins/aks-desktop/src/telemetry`. Deployed clients emit **two different event shapes**; every query below normalizes across both. See `docs/telemetry/README.md` for the schema, the client-shape discriminator, and the caveat behind each tile.

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
let ev = customEvents
| extend build = case(name !in (envelopes), 'legacy', array_length(bag_keys(customDimensions)) == 0, 'legacy', 'current')
| where '{ClientFilter}' == 'all' or build == '{ClientFilter}';
ev
| summarize
    Sessions = dcount(session_Id),
    Installs = dcountif(user_Id, build == 'current'),
    Legacy = dcountif(user_Id, build == 'legacy'),
    Events = count()
| extend p = pack('Sessions', Sessions, 'Installs (current build)', Installs, 'Legacy clients (approx.)', Legacy, 'Events', Events)
| mv-expand kind=array p
| project Metric = tostring(p[0]), Value = toint(p[1])
content.title: At a glance

content.json: **Installs** counts `user_Id`, which the current build stamps with the stable `installId` UUID. Legacy clients never set it, so their `user_Id` is SDK-generated and rotates — that column is an upper-bound device estimate, not an install count. The two are deliberately not summed.

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
customEvents
| extend build = case(name !in (envelopes), 'legacy', array_length(bag_keys(customDimensions)) == 0, 'legacy', 'current')
| where build == 'current'
| summarize ['Active installs'] = dcount(user_Id), Sessions = dcount(session_Id) by bin(timestamp, 1d)
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: Daily active installs and sessions (current build only)

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
let sv = customEvents
| where name == 'headlamp.session-start'
| summarize SessionAppVersion = max(tostring(customDimensions.appVersion)) by session_Id;
customEvents
| extend build = case(name !in (envelopes), 'legacy', array_length(bag_keys(customDimensions)) == 0, 'legacy', 'current')
| join kind=leftouter sv on session_Id
| extend AppVersion = coalesce(tostring(customDimensions.appVersion), SessionAppVersion, iff(build == 'legacy', 'legacy build', 'unknown'))
| summarize Sessions = dcount(session_Id) by bin(timestamp, 1d), AppVersion
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: Version rollout — are installs moving off the legacy build?

content.json: The deployed build only puts `appVersion` on `headlamp.session-start`, so this tile resolves each event's version by joining back to its session rather than reading the dimension per-event. The `coalesce` also reads a per-event `appVersion` first, so it keeps working unchanged once the current code (which stamps every envelope in `send()`) ships.

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
let cur = customEvents
| where timestamp > ago(90d)
| extend build = case(name !in (envelopes), 'legacy', array_length(bag_keys(customDimensions)) == 0, 'legacy', 'current')
| where build == 'current';
let firstSeen = cur
| summarize firstSeen = min(timestamp) by user_Id;
cur
| where timestamp between ({TimeRange:start} .. {TimeRange:end})
| summarize by user_Id, day = bin(timestamp, 1d)
| join kind=leftouter firstSeen on user_Id
| extend cohort = iff(bin(firstSeen, 1d) >= day, 'New', 'Returning')
| summarize Installs = dcount(user_Id) by day, cohort
| order by day asc
content.title: New vs returning installs (90-day lookback)

content.json: This tile deliberately ignores the time-range parameter for its lookback — it needs 90 days of history to tell a genuinely new install from a returning one, so it filters on `{TimeRange:start}`/`{TimeRange:end}` in KQL instead. It is current-build only (legacy `user_Id` rotates, which would fake an endless stream of new installs). An install first seen before the 90-day window reads as _Returning_.

content.query:
customEvents
| where name == 'headlamp.session-start'
| summarize Sessions = count(), Installs = dcount(user_Id) by
    OS = tostring(customDimensions.os),
    Arch = tostring(customDimensions.arch),
    Electron = tostring(customDimensions.electronVersion),
    Locale = tostring(customDimensions.locale)
| order by Sessions desc
content.title: Environment mix (session-start; current build only)

content.query:
customEvents
| where name == 'headlamp.plugins-loaded'
| where array_length(bag_keys(customDimensions)) > 0
| extend
    Total = toint(customDimensions.totalCount),
    Enabled = toint(customDimensions.enabledCount),
    ThirdParty = toint(customDimensions.thirdPartyCount),
    AksdEnabled = iff(tostring(customDimensions.knownEnabledIds) has 'aks-desktop', 'yes', 'no')
| summarize Sessions = dcount(session_Id) by Total, Enabled, ThirdParty, AksdEnabled
| order by Sessions desc
content.title: Plugin load-out — is the AKS plugin actually enabled?

content.json: `knownEnabledIds` is filtered against `KNOWN_PLUGIN_IDS` before sending, so it only ever contains `aks-desktop` — third-party plugin names are never transmitted, only counted (`index.ts:385`). `AksdEnabled = no` with a healthy `Enabled` count means the user is running Headlamp with the AKS plugin switched off.

Funnels cover the three AKS-specific flows: **project-create**, **project-import** and **deploy**. Stages count _distinct sessions reaching that status_, not raw events, so a user retrying inside one session is counted once.

Only the current build carries a `status` dimension, so these tiles are effectively current-build only regardless of the client filter.

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
let ev = customEvents
| extend build = case(name !in (envelopes), 'legacy', array_length(bag_keys(customDimensions)) == 0, 'legacy', 'current')
| where '{ClientFilter}' == 'all' or build == '{ClientFilter}'
| extend feature = iff(name == 'headlamp.feature', tostring(customDimensions.feature), iff(name in (envelopes), '', name)), status = coalesce(tostring(customDimensions.status), 'unknown');
ev
| where feature startswith 'aksd.'
| summarize
    Opened = dcountif(session_Id, status == 'opened'),
    Started = dcountif(session_Id, status == 'started'),
    Succeeded = dcountif(session_Id, status == 'succeeded'),
    Partial = dcountif(session_Id, status == 'completed'),
    Failed = dcountif(session_Id, status == 'failed'),
    Cancelled = dcountif(session_Id, status == 'cancelled')
  by Funnel = feature
| extend ['Start rate %'] = iff(Opened == 0, todouble(''), round(100.0 * Started / todouble(Opened), 1))
| extend ['Success rate %'] = iff(Started == 0, todouble(''), round(100.0 * (Succeeded + Partial) / todouble(Started), 1))
| order by Funnel asc
content.title: Funnel conversion by flow

content.json:
`aksd.project-import` reports `completed` when _some_ namespaces imported and others failed (`ImportAKSProjects.tsx:383`). It is folded into **Success rate** alongside `succeeded` but broken out as **Partial** — a rising Partial column is a real regression a plain success rate would hide.

`aksd.deploy` emits `opened` from `DeployButton` and `started`/`succeeded`/`failed` from the wizard. It has **no `cancelled` path**, so abandonment shows only as `opened` with no terminal status — expect its Start rate to read lower than the other two flows for reasons that are not a UX problem.

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
customEvents
| extend feature = iff(name == 'headlamp.feature', tostring(customDimensions.feature), iff(name in (envelopes), '', name)), status = coalesce(tostring(customDimensions.status), 'unknown')
| where feature startswith 'aksd.'
| where status in ('succeeded', 'completed', 'failed', 'cancelled')
| summarize Sessions = dcount(session_Id) by status, feature
| order by Sessions desc
content.title: Terminal outcomes by flow

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
customEvents
| extend feature = iff(name == 'headlamp.feature', tostring(customDimensions.feature), iff(name in (envelopes), '', name)), status = coalesce(tostring(customDimensions.status), 'unknown')
| where feature startswith 'aksd.'
| summarize
    Started = dcountif(session_Id, status == 'started'),
    Succeeded = dcountif(session_Id, status in ('succeeded', 'completed'))
  by bin(timestamp, 1d)
| extend ['Success rate %'] = iff(Started == 0, todouble(''), round(100.0 * Succeeded / todouble(Started), 1))
| project timestamp, ['Success rate %']
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: Success rate over time (all AKS flows)
Silent drop-off — flows started that never reported an outcome

content.json: A session that reaches `started` but never reports a terminal status means the app was closed or crashed mid-flow, or the terminal-tracking guard (`terminalTrackedRef`) never fired. This is the one funnel signal that a plain conversion rate cannot show, because the session simply vanishes from the denominator's numerator rather than appearing as a failure.

> **Read event counts here as a floor, not a total.** `trackError` drops everything past **5 events per `area:errorClass` per session** (`telemetry/index.ts:56`). _Sessions affected_ is the trustworthy measure; _Events_ is censored and will flatten out exactly when things are going worst.

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
let ev = customEvents
| extend build = case(name !in (envelopes), 'legacy', array_length(bag_keys(customDimensions)) == 0, 'legacy', 'current')
| where '{ClientFilter}' == 'all' or build == '{ClientFilter}';
ev
| summarize
    Total = dcount(session_Id),
    Affected = dcountif(session_Id, name == 'headlamp.exception')
| extend ErrorFree = iff(Total == 0, todouble(''), round(100.0 * (Total - Affected) / todouble(Total), 1))
| extend p = pack('Sessions', todouble(Total), 'Sessions with an error', todouble(Affected), 'Error-free %', ErrorFree)
| mv-expand kind=array p
| project Metric = tostring(p[0]), Value = todouble(p[1])
content.title: Session health

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
let ev = customEvents
| extend build = case(name !in (envelopes), 'legacy', array_length(bag_keys(customDimensions)) == 0, 'legacy', 'current')
| where '{ClientFilter}' == 'all' or build == '{ClientFilter}';
ev
| where name == 'headlamp.exception'
| summarize
    ['Sessions affected'] = dcount(session_Id),
    ['Installs affected'] = dcount(user_Id),
    ['Events (capped)'] = count()
  by
    Area = tostring(customDimensions.area),
    ['Error class'] = tostring(customDimensions.errorClass),
    Phase = coalesce(tostring(customDimensions.phase), '(none)')
| order by ['Sessions affected'] desc
content.title: Errors by area, class and phase

content.json:
`area` is one of `project-create`, `project-import`, `deploy`, `kubernetes`, `plugin-ui`. Anything in **`plugin-ui`** came from `TelemetryErrorBoundary` and is hard-coded to `UnknownError` / `failed` (`TelemetryErrorBoundary.tsx:41`) — a React render crash, not a classified failure. Treat a spike there as "go read the boundary", not as a diagnosis.

`deploy` failures are only ever `ValidationError` or `UnknownError`; the wizard has no other classification, so do not read the absence of `NetworkError` as evidence the network is healthy.

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
let ev = customEvents
| extend build = case(name !in (envelopes), 'legacy', array_length(bag_keys(customDimensions)) == 0, 'legacy', 'current')
| where '{ClientFilter}' == 'all' or build == '{ClientFilter}';
ev
| summarize
    Total = dcount(session_Id),
    Affected = dcountif(session_Id, name == 'headlamp.exception')
  by bin(timestamp, 1d)
| extend ['Sessions affected %'] = iff(Total == 0, todouble(''), round(100.0 * Affected / todouble(Total), 1))
| project timestamp, ['Sessions affected %']
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: Share of sessions hitting an error, over time

content.query:
let sv = customEvents
| where name == 'headlamp.session-start'
| summarize SessionAppVersion = max(tostring(customDimensions.appVersion)) by session_Id;
let errs = customEvents
| where name == 'headlamp.exception'
| extend Area = tostring(customDimensions.area);
let sessions = customEvents
| summarize by session_Id;
errs
| join kind=leftouter sv on session_Id
| extend ['App version'] = coalesce(tostring(customDimensions.appVersion), SessionAppVersion, 'unknown')
| summarize ['Sessions affected'] = dcount(session_Id) by Area, ['App version']
| order by ['Sessions affected'] desc
content.title: Errors by app version — did a release make things worse?

content.json: Raw affected-session counts, not rates — a version with more installs will show more errors. Compare against **Daily active installs** on the Adoption tab before concluding a release regressed. `unknown` means the session's `session-start` fell outside the selected time range, which is common for long-running desktop sessions.

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
let ev = customEvents
| extend build = case(name !in (envelopes), 'legacy', array_length(bag_keys(customDimensions)) == 0, 'legacy', 'current')
| where '{ClientFilter}' == 'all' or build == '{ClientFilter}'
| extend feature = iff(name == 'headlamp.feature', tostring(customDimensions.feature), iff(name in (envelopes), '', name));
ev
| where isnotempty(feature)
| summarize
    Sessions = dcount(session_Id),
    ['Current-build installs'] = dcountif(user_Id, build == 'current'),
    Events = count()
  by Feature = feature
| order by Sessions desc
| take 30
content.title: Feature usage — normalized across both client shapes

content.json: `headlamp.list-view`, `headlamp.details-view` and `headlamp.object-events` fire on **render**, not on a deliberate click, and re-fire on re-render — the sample data shows a dozen within one second for a single navigation. **Rank features by _Sessions_, never by _Events_**; the Events column measures render churn, not intent, and is useful mainly for spotting a re-render bug.

content.query:
customEvents
| where name == 'headlamp.feature'
| extend Feature = tostring(customDimensions.feature), ResourceKind = tostring(customDimensions.resourceKind)
| where isnotempty(ResourceKind)
| summarize Sessions = dcount(session_Id) by ResourceKind, Feature
| order by Sessions desc
| take 40
content.title: Which resource kinds do people act on? (current build only)

content.json: `resourceKind` is clamped to the built-in Kubernetes kind list; anything else collapses to **`CustomResource`**, and heterogeneous bulk actions report **`Multiple`** (`schema.ts:182`). You cannot recover which CRD was involved — that is by design, not a gap to fix.

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
let ev = customEvents
| extend build = case(name !in (envelopes), 'legacy', array_length(bag_keys(customDimensions)) == 0, 'legacy', 'current')
| where '{ClientFilter}' == 'all' or build == '{ClientFilter}';
ev
| summarize
    Total = dcount(session_Id),
    WithShape = dcountif(session_Id, name == 'headlamp.cluster-shape')
| extend Coverage = iff(Total == 0, todouble(''), round(100.0 * WithShape / todouble(Total), 1))
| extend p = pack('Sessions', todouble(Total), 'Reporting cluster shape', todouble(WithShape), 'Coverage %', Coverage)
| mv-expand kind=array p
| project Metric = tostring(p[0]), Value = todouble(p[1])
content.title: Cluster-shape coverage

content.json: Read this tile **before** the three below it. `trackClusterShape` emits nothing unless _all five_ of k8s version, node count, namespace count, region and tier are non-null, and it dedupes to once per cluster per process (`telemetry/index.ts:312`). Low coverage has two very different causes — nobody opened an AKS cluster, or one ARM field came back null — and the distributions below are only representative to the degree this number is high. In the sample hour, coverage was **zero**.

content.query:
customEvents
| where name == 'headlamp.cluster-shape'
| summarize Clusters = count() by ['Kubernetes minor'] = tostring(customDimensions.kubernetesMinor)
| order by ['Kubernetes minor'] asc
content.title: Kubernetes minor version

content.query:
customEvents
| where name == 'headlamp.cluster-shape'
| summarize Clusters = count() by Tier = tostring(customDimensions.aksTier)
| order by Clusters desc
content.title: AKS tier

content.query:
customEvents
| where name == 'headlamp.cluster-shape'
| summarize Clusters = count() by
    Region = tostring(customDimensions.region),
    Nodes = tostring(customDimensions.nodeCountBucket),
    Namespaces = tostring(customDimensions.namespaceCountBucket)
| order by Clusters desc
content.title: Region and cluster size buckets

content.json: `region` passes a shape check rather than an allowlist, so unrecognized values land in **`Other`** (`schema.ts:192`). Node and namespace counts are bucketed client-side — `0`, `1-5`, `6-20`, `21-100`, `100+` and `0`, `1-10`, `11-50`, `51-200`, `200+` — and the raw counts are never sent, so no finer breakdown is recoverable.

content.query:
let envelopes = dynamic(['headlamp.session-start','headlamp.feature','headlamp.exception','headlamp.cluster-shape','headlamp.plugins-loaded']);
customEvents
| extend build = case(name !in (envelopes), 'legacy', array_length(bag_keys(customDimensions)) == 0, 'legacy', 'current')
| where build == 'current'
| summarize Events = count(), Sessions = dcount(session_Id) by Route = coalesce(operation_Name, '(none)')
| order by Events desc
content.title: Sanitized route distribution (current build only)

content.json: A large `unknown` bucket is expected, not a bug: `sanitizeRoute` maps anything outside the fixed route allowlist to `unknown` (`schema.ts:206`), and every Kubernetes resource route falls outside it. Legacy clients are excluded here because they report a raw `file://` install path instead of a route — which is exactly what the sanitizer was added to stop.
